title: Modernization and Engineering Support - III (MES III)
description: The Air National Guard (ANG) Air Force Reserve Command Test Center (AATC) is a unit of the ANG stationed at Tucson Air National Guard Base (ANGB), AZ with operating locations at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base (AFB), AZ; Eglin AFB, FL; Little Rock AFB, AR; Roland R. Wright ANGB, UT; and Hancock Field ANGB, NY. AATC conducts operational test and evaluation (OT&E) for the Air Reserve Component (ARC) and other Major Commands (MAJCOMs) exercising lead command authority over a variety of ARC possessed Mission Design Series (MDS) systems and associated weapons, sensors, and support equipment. These ARC aircraft and systems are older and require low cost, off-the-shelf modernization updates to maintain combat capabilities. AATC has engineering and test responsibility for the National Guard Bureau (NGB) and Air Force Reserve Command (AFRC). In this role, AATC is responsible for working with Air Force Material Command (AFMC), system program offices (SPOs), and other related engineering offices to conduct research, development, test, and evaluation to determine the operational suitability and effectiveness of candidate developmental sensors and systems that address the modernization requirements identified in the annual Air National Guard Weapons System Modernization Priorities Book, and Air Force Reserve Modernization Book as well as requirements provided to AATC by the MAJCOMs. There are currently over 100 active projects at AATC supporting A-10, C-130, F-15, F-35, F-16, C-17, KC-135, KC-46, HH-60, HC/MC-130, MQ-9, Special Warfare (SW), Cyber, and multiple cross-platform logistics and electronic warfare (EW) capabilities. The average lifetime of most projects is six months to three years from concept approval to final report and initial fielding, but complexity may shorten or extend the amount of time required to complete the project. Expertise for each of these platforms and capability areas is required to ensure successful testing of modernization capabilities. Skill set requirements may be transferable or adjusted as projects are completed and new projects are started. Required technical expertise includes but is not limited to: operational and maintenance experience on specific platforms, expertise or familiarization with platform systems, integration and modification experience, developmental and operational test experience, airworthiness and Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) approvals, assisting the Government with technical requirements definition, cost assessment and control, executing aircraft avionics integration, systems engineering, design engineering, creating integrated logistics support such as technical orders, flight manuals, job guides, and software manuals, and program engineering coordination necessary to support ANG and AFRC modification programs. New projects may need additional expertise as they are approved in the annual United States Air Force Reserve Modernization Book and ANG Weapons Systems Modernization Priorities Book. These books are available online and identify modernization priorities and projects this PWS will support. As modernization priorities and projects are approved and funded, AATC will conduct OT&E activities to determine the validity of solutions and make fielding recommendations, as required. The contractor will support this process through all phases from concept development, test planning, test execution, and final report delivery. The ability to develop briefings, write test plans, conduct tests, and deliver comprehensive final reports is required. The contractor shall perform test planning, test execution, data analysis, test reporting, test logistics and studies/analysis for modernization installations and integration on ARC platforms which are composed of the ANG and AFRC weapons systems. In addition, the contractor shall perform specialized System Under Test (SUT) acquisition, program management, integration engineering, engineering liaison, and technology insertion to assist AATC and NGB/A5 with modernization of ARC weapons systems to include but not limited to aircraft, Joint Terminal Area Controller (JTAC) and Special Warfare, Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (C4ISR), domestic operations, cyber security, logistics programs software support, and test process training support. ARC modernization efforts require avionics, mechanical, and structural modifications to include but not limited to technical requirements definition, avionics integration, systems engineering, design engineering, test support, integrated logistics engineering, studies and analyses, cybersecurity approval, prototype installations, program engineering coordination, test equipment, and technical documentation. Participation in integrated product teams (IPTs) within the Department of Defense (DoD) communities will be required to accomplish the assigned tasks. The products and support will be provided to several customers including AATC, MAJCOMs, Air Force and other DoD stakeholders to include the Aeronautical Systems Center (ASC) and Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) supported programs, Air Force Life Cycle Management Centers (AFLCM) program offices, and Joint Program Offices (JPO).

description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA) Management & Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking an Expression of Interest (EOI) from qualified vendors to provide replacement services for rollup doors at the Specific Manufacturing Capability (SMC) facility. This initiative supports BEA�s commitment to maintaining secure and efficient access points for operational areas. BACKGROUND Due to failures and obsolesces, the SMC facility requires replacement of several exterior and interior aging rollup doors to ensure proper functionality, security, and compliance with safety standards. The scope of work may include the following: Removal and disposal of existing rollup doors and hardware. Installation of new rollup doors and associated components. Verification of alignment, operation, and safety features. Compliance with applicable DOE, safety, and building standards. Testing and commissioning to confirm proper functionality. INL is a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratory dedicated to nuclear energy, national security, and clean energy innovation. INL is operated under a management and operating contract with the Department of Energy and as such, the Davis-Bacon Act applies for contracts in excess of $2,000 for the construction, alteration, or repair (including painting and decorating) of buildings or works at INL. Construction work at the laboratory Site covered under the Davis-Bacon Act is additionally subject to the INL Site Stabilization Agreement (SSA). These Site areas include all areas within the 890-square mile boundary, including the Material and Fuels Complex, Central Facilities Area, Advanced Test Reactor, Radioactive Waste Management Complex, and Specific Manufacturing Capability. The agreement is between signatory contractors and labor unions performing such work. Information regarding the INL Site Stabilization Agreement is available from the Site Labor Coordinator at (208) 524-4404 or at lance@sitelabor.org. Construction work performed at Idaho Falls facilities is not subject to these agreements. PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. description: East Suffolk and North Essex NHS Foundation Trust (ESNEFT) is inviting qualified Suppliers to express an interest to participate in a tender exercise for; Charitable Funds Investment under the Procurement Act 2023. This expression of interest will require interested parties to: - Confirm interest - Complete and submit capability assessment attachment The Capability Assessment submitted by interested parties will be reviewed to identify appropriate Suppliers to invite to tender. Invitation to Tender (ITT) with project timelines to be issued upon successful pass of this Capability Assessment stage. The Trust will aim to issue the ITT in October 2026. The top four suppliers, based on the evaluation of their ITT submissions, will be invited to interview with the Trust. Accordingly, all suppliers should be advised that interviews are provisionally scheduled for the afternoon of 16 November 2026. As this date has been agreed with key stakeholders, it is not expected to change. East Suffolk and North Essex NHS Foundation Trust (ESNEFT) is the largest NHS organisation in its region, formed on July 1, 2018, through the merger of Colchester Hospital University NHS Foundation Trust and The Ipswich Hospital NHS Trust. ESNEFT provides comprehensive hospital and community healthcare services across multiple locations, including Colchester, Ipswich, Clacton, Halstead, Harwich, Felixstowe, and Aldeburgh. The trust offers a wide range of medical services such as acute medicine, cardiology, dermatology, emergency assessment, gastroenterology, neurology, and many more. ESNEFT is committed to delivering high-quality care and continuously improving its facilities and services to meet the needs of the local communities. Every year hundreds of individuals, community groups and businesses generously donate money to help us achieve our aims. It is our job to make sure that the money is spent carefully and for the purposes for which it was given. The ESNEFT Charity holds designated charitable funds for many of the services in the hospital as well as appeal funds. They have a duty to maximise the value it gets from public donation, but without exposure to undue levels of risk. We do not have the skills in house therefore appoint advisors to assist us with this. The Charity's existing portfolio is invested in Ethical investment funds, property funds and a common deposit fund. ESNEFT is looking to re-procure the management and advice of The Trusts Charitable Funds Investment. title: Canonsburg-Houston, Pennsylvania, Local Protection Project (LPP) PL84-99 Rehabilitation
description: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE DISCLAIMER: This document is issued solely for informational and planning purposes as a Presolicitation Notice and does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ), or a promise to issue an award or solicitation in the future. The information and requirements outlined herein are subject to change. Specifications, drawings, schedules, wage rate determinations, and solicitation instructions will be provided upon the official posting of the formal RFQ. 1. Project Overview & Background The Canonsburg-Houston Local Protection Project (LPP) is an authorized federal flood damage reduction project spanning over 20,500 linear feet of channel improvements along Chartiers Creek. Originally constructed by USACE in two phases (Houston unit completed in 1970; Canonsburg unit completed in 1976), operation and maintenance responsibilities were subsequently transferred to Washington County. Severe storm events resulted in substantial damage to the channel embankment along the right bank of Chartiers Creek, including displacement of stone protection and loss of subgrade stabilization. This rehabilitation contract encompasses repair and re-armoring of the degraded channel reach to restore federal project integrity and design conveyance capacity. The Anticipated Cost of Construction is between $150,000.00 and $300,000.00. The project is to be completed within 120 Calendar Days after written Notice to Proceed (NTP). 2. Technical Scope of Work & Execution Limits The contractor must furnish all management, supervision, labor, heavy equipment, materials, water control, and environmental controls necessary to execute the repairs. Repair Reach Limits: Repair work is concentrated along the right bank of Chartiers Creek between approximate stations STA 164+00 and STA 166+50. Site Access & Clearing: Access to the creek channel will be achieved from the left bank access ramp near STA 163+00. The ramp requires clearing of dense brush and vegetation in strict accordance with PennDOT Publication 408, Section 201. Geotextile Underlayment: Existing geotextiles within the damage limits are assumed damaged and must be excavated and replaced. The contractor must furnish and place Class 4, Type A non-woven geotextile fabric conforming to PennDOT 408 Section 735. Panels must be placed over prepared, compacted subgrade with a minimum 18-inch overlap, placing upstream panels over downstream panels. Stone Protection (R-5 Riprap): Riprap protection will be restored using PennDOT R-5 stone (minimum 1�-6� layer thickness) conforming to PennDOT 408 Section 850 and ASTM D5519. Stones must be placed with zero free fall and a maximum drop height not exceeding 12 inches to prevent fabric puncturing and stone segregation. Hand or mechanical rearrangement is required to achieve a dense, evenly graded mass free of stone clusters or void pockets. Temporary Water Diversion & Dewatering: In-channel work must be performed in completely dewatered conditions. The contractor is responsible for the complete engineering, installation, continuous pumping/diversion, maintenance, and final removal of a temporary water diversion system. All pumped effluent must pass through certified sediment/debris control devices prior to discharge back into the creek. Removed streambed material must be stockpiled and replaced upon completion. Demolition & Waste Disposal: Damaged geotextile, dead vegetative matter, and unserviceable excavated fill must be excavated, loaded, and disposed of off-site at a commercially permitted landfill or recycling facility in accordance with PADEP 258-2182-773 (Management of Fill). 3. Key Personnel & Qualification Thresholds On-site supervisory staff must satisfy strict USACE qualifications and maintain designated physical presence: Project Superintendent: Minimum of 5 years of construction experience, including at least 5 years serving as superintendent on comparable earthwork and channel restoration projects. Must possess demonstrated proficiency in USACE EM 385-1-1 safety compliance and hazard mitigation. Dedicated role; cannot serve concurrently as the QCSM or SSHO. Contractor Quality Control System Manager (QCSM): Minimum of 5 years of construction experience on similar stream restoration and civil earthwork projects. Must be directly employed by the prime contractor and hold a valid Construction Quality Management for Contractors (CQM-C) certification issued by USACE/NAVFAC. Required to be on site at all times during construction activities. Site Safety and Health Officer (SSHO): Must meet Level 1 SSHO qualifications outlined in EM 385-1-1 (2024 edition) and be formally designated via ENG Form 6282. Full-time responsibility reporting directly to a corporate officer; must be on-site whenever active operations occur. Dual-Hat Allowance: The SSHO may concurrently serve as the QCSM (provided all CQM-C requirements are satisfied) but cannot serve as the Project Superintendent. Safety Compliance: Safety Compliance (EM 385-1-1): Offerors are advised that all work on this project must strictly comply with the latest edition of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Safety and Health Requirements Manual (EM 385-1-1) (Link: https://www.publications.usace.army.mil/Portals/76/EM%20385-1-1%20_EFFECTIVE%2015March2024.pdf). Prior to commencing work, the contractor must submit and secure Government approval for a site-specific Accident Prevention Plan (APP) and comprehensive Activity Hazard Analyses (AHAs). 4. Key Performance Constraints & Operational Rules 25-Foot Embankment Exposure Limit: To prevent catastrophic washout during sudden high streamflows, the contractor must limit stripped subgrade or exposed geotextile fabric to maximum 25-foot linear sections, or lengths that can be fully backfilled and armored with R-5 riprap within the same working shift. Embankments covered solely by geotextile fabric are formally classified as unprotected. NWS Weather Monitoring & High-Water Action Thresholds: The contractor must continuously monitor National Weather Service (NWS) hydrologic forecasts for the Chartiers Creek tributary basin. Upon the issuance of any NWS Flash Flood Watch or Flash Flood Warning, all in-channel operations must be immediately suspended, equipment evacuated to high ground, and incremental work secured. Protection of Incremental Work: Work must be sequenced so that initiated features can be completed, stabilized, or protected prior to forecasted high-water events. Any equipment, materials, or partially installed work damaged by stream currents or inadequate water diversion must be replaced at the contractor�s expense. 5. The anticipated award date is 13 November 2026. The basis of award will be of best value to the Government. Basis of Award is best value to the Government. title: ETHEREAL FORGE: Call for Participation � Test & Evaluation of Advanced Electromagnetic Warfare (EW) Capabilities
description: Overall objective: Test and evaluate Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA)-conformant, modular, advanced Electromagnetic Warfare (EW) capabilities against realistic threats in a representative environment to assess capability utility, inform the development and acquisitions processes, and gain insight to support rapid, iterative fielding of Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations (EMSO) capabilities. The objective is to be a forcing function to drive towards the next generation of modular, rapidly upgradeable EMSO systems that will sense the electromagnetic environment, make sense of it, maneuver within it, and engage with precision at the speed of light. Background: Many promising EW capabilities are being developed based on modular hardware- and software-centric principles linked to mature open standards, such as SOSA, CMOSS, FACE, VITA, and/or AMS-GRA. These capabilities require demonstration in a representative environment before being accepted by program offices for final integration. This event will leverage lessons learned from multiple pathfinding events, experiments, and exercises over the past six years. Expected outcomes: Technology Readiness Assessments of the suitability for further integration and fielding of candidate capabilities (specifically software applications and SOSA hardware components) Key data to support future budgeting cycles and acquisition processes Data-centric assessments to inform mission- and campaign-level simulations, directly supporting long-term planning and acquisitions cycles Prototype infrastructure and process to accelerate test and evaluation of modular hardware components and software-defined capabilities

title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/ SOURCES SOUGHT Space Force Mission Delta 9 (MD9) � SL-5 EC2-S Ground System Sustainment
description: DESCRIPTION: MD 9 is seeking market research information for an enterprise Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) in accordance with DFARS 212.70, Defense Commercial Solutions Opening. The goal is to enhance MD 9�s operational capabilities through innovative commercial solutions to acquire innovative commercial products, technologies, or services. Headquarters is located at Schriever Space Force Base, Colorado, and is the United States Space Force's designated orbital warfare organization. Its core purpose is to guarantee the United States, and its allies have undisputed freedom of action in space. The mission of MD9 is to prepare, present, and project assigned and attached forces for the purpose of conducting protect and defend operations while providing national decision authorities with response options to deter and, when necessary, defeat orbital threats. Additionally, MD9 supports Space Domain Awareness by conducting space-based battlespace characterization operations and conducts on-orbit experimentation and technology demonstrations for the USSF. To achieve this, MD 9 is comprised of specialized units, including space operations squadrons responsible for on-orbit engagements, while also being supported by dedicated cyber, intelligence, and sustainment squadrons that ensure the availability, reliability, security, and effectiveness of its mission systems. RFI and/or Sources Sought: The Government is conducting market research to inform an enterprise acquisition strategy for the Mission Delta 9 (MD9) effort. This effort is intended to support the full MD9 enterprise and is not limited to a single Area of Interest (AOI) or specific requirement. Individual AOIs may involve varying security levels and access requirements based on their respective operational, technical, and acquisition considerations. At this time, the Government is requesting: Review and inputs on the unclassified enterprise Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) Completion of the Initial Intake RFI Questionnaire; and Submission of an unclassified Capability Statement from all interested organizations. Completion of the questionnaire is necessary to obtain sufficient market-research information and assess the number of industry partners capable of responding to various AOIs that may be issued at differing security levels. The anticipated effort includes support at multiple locations, including Kirtland Air Force Base, New Mexico This RFI/Sources Sought Information request has been reaccomplished to capture adequate information from Industry. If you have submitted a capability statement already, you are not required to resubmit. 22 Sep 2026 Overhaul of the RFI/Sources Sought Information effort. Released the Draft enterprise CSO for review. Please provide responses by 11 Oct 2026. DISCLAIMER & IMPORTANT NOTES: This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This RFI does not commit the US Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. All submissions will become Government property and will not be returned.
